result.target_summary: While Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in certain jurisdictions effective for fiscal year 2025, NVIDIA does not expect a material impact on its effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, though new guidance could change this assessment.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure addresses the impact of Pillar Two global minimum tax legislation enacted for FY2025, stating no material impact is expected. This is a new regulatory development not present in the 2023 Item 7 disclosures, which focus on TCJA R&D capitalization (D067), FDII/stock-based compensation benefits (D066, D068), and general effective tax rate drivers. No 2023 counterpart regarding Pillar Two exists in the required IDs.

current_disclosures.summary: While Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in certain jurisdictions effective for fiscal year 2025, NVIDIA does not expect a material impact on its effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, though new guidance could change this assessment.

materiality_analysis.reason: This is an introduced disclosure addressing the impact of new global minimum tax legislation (Pillar Two) effective in 2025. Although NVIDIA states no material impact is currently expected, the disclosure of a new regulatory regime and the explicit disclaimer that 'new guidance could change this assessment' introduces a new forward-looking risk and compliance consideration not previously present.

The disclosure represents a temporal shift in reporting cycles rather than a material change in tax risk or regulatory exposure. comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Pillar Two on company's 2024 financials
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of Pillar Two legislation on the company for the fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, and the company continues to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose the impact of OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax legislation on their financials for fiscal year 2024, concluding that the effect was immaterial or not expected to be material on their effective tax rates and cash flows. While NVIDIA states it does not expect a material impact in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, AMD explicitly confirms that for fiscal 2024, the impact was immaterial. Both companies also note that they are actively evaluating new guidance and legislation as it becomes available, which could change their assessments.

sentences.text: Based on enacted laws, Pillar Two is not expected to materially impact our effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year.

The OECD, and its member countries, continue to release new guidance and legislation on Pillar Two and we continue to evaluate the impact on our financial position of the global implementation of these rules.
For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.
We continue to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes to our effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax implementation status
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD is continuing discussions on profit allocation and global minimum tax (Pillar One and Two), with the EU having adopted the 15% minimum tax for member states and many other countries implementing laws with effective dates starting in 2024, though some jurisdictions where the company operates have not yet adopted corresponding legislation.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the implementation status of the OECD Pillar Two 15% global minimum tax and the adoption of legislation by specific jurisdictions like the EU and UK. NVIDIA notes that jurisdictions including EU member states and the UK have enacted legislation effective for fiscal year 2025, while AMD details that the EU has adopted the 15% minimum tax and many non-EU countries have implemented laws with effective dates starting in 2024. Both companies acknowledge that certain jurisdictions where they operate have not yet adopted corresponding legislation.

sentences.text: Certain jurisdictions, including European Union member states and the United Kingdom, have enacted Pillar Two legislation that will start to become effective for our fiscal year 2025.
The Council of the European Union has adopted the global corporate 15% minimum tax as provided for in Pillar Two and has directed EU member states to implement legislation enacting Pillar Two.
Many countries, including non-EU member states, have implemented laws based on Pillar Two proposals, with effective dates that started in 2024.

Although many countries have already introduced Pillar Two legislation applicable to us effective in 2024, certain jurisdictions in which we operate have not adopted corresponding legislation to date.
